title: driver-lib-shadowing-timeline-probes
content:
Quick note: this is a working scratchpad for a weird OOM that only happens inside certain containers on one host (prod-gpu-12). Not a final writeup.

Situation summary:
- Symptoms: intermittent (but reproducible on demand) CUDA OOMs during batch inference startup. Works fine on other hosts. Failures started after an image push and pip/conda package update.
- Hypothesis: dynamic library shadowing (different libcudart / libcuda / libnvrtc loaded from user image vs host driver) causing allocator mismatch and stale NVML handles -> inaccurate free space and immediate OOM.

Host details (prod-gpu-12):
- kernel: 5.15.0-89-generic
- nvidia-driver: 535.54 (from apt-ubuntu-driver package)
- nvidia-smi: shows driver 535.54, 4x A100-SXM4 80GB
- docker runtime: nvidia-container-runtime 2.11.0

Image in question: registry.redwood.internal/rt-inference:v2026-02-10
- base: nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04
- python: 3.10.13
- conda: not used for failing image (pip-only)

Timeline / repro probes (ordered):
1) 2026-02-15 09:12 - first noticed after deploy of v2026-02-10. Repro: run unit batch script (start-server -> load model -> warmup batch). Fails during warmup with CUDA OOM.

2) 2026-02-15 09:30 - quick check on worker: nvidia-smi during failure shows all GPUs with 1-2GB used, then process spikes allocation and OOM. But host free GPU memory (according to nvidia-smi) should be >70GB, so mismatch.

Commands tried and outputs:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
  -> shows memory usages as expected when container not started.

- docker run --rm -it --gpus all registry.redwood.internal/rt-inference:v2026-02-10 bash
  Inside container: python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); a=torch.randn(2,2, device='cuda')"
  -> torch.cuda.is_available() -> True
  -> small tensor alloc OK

- python script that grabs large tensor: python -c "import torch; x=torch.empty(40_000_000, dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda'); print('ok')"
  -> inside failing container on prod-gpu-12: CUDA out of memory or driver not responding depending on run. Same command inside identical image on prod-gpu-03: works.

- ldd $(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__file__)')/lib/torch.so  (approx)
  -> noted that libtorch links to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 which is provided by the host driver via /usr/lib/nvidia

- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import torch; x=torch.zeros(1,device='cuda')" 2>&1 | grep cuda
  -> observed two distinct paths: one from /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib and a secondary libcuda coming from /opt/cuda/lib64 inside the image (leftover from base image), plus host-provided driver. This looked suspicious: mixed runtimes.

Kernel logs during one crash (dmesg excerpt):
- [ 2378.123456] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU-...
- [ 2378.123458] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=24192, name=python
- [ 2378.123459] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79: GPU has fallen off the bus.

This points to low-level driver issues rather than pure allocator OOM. But interestingly the Python traceback in logs came back as CUDA OOM. Mixed symptoms.

Additional probes done:
- inspect container image: find / -name "libcuda*" -> found /usr/local/cuda-12.0/compat/libcuda.so symlink (leftover).
- strace -f -e open,read python -c "import torch; torch.zeros(1, device='cuda')"
  -> open("/usr/local/cuda-12.0/compat/libcuda.so", O_RDONLY) succeeded, then later host /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 also opened. Double-open implies both compat shim and host driver present.

Hypothesis refinement:
- If the container image includes compatibility stubs or older libcuda shipped in /usr/local/cuda/... they can be picked up before the host's runtime libs depending on LD_LIBRARY_PATH or rpath. If the user-level libcuda is not ABI-compatible with the driver, NVML or CUDA contexts can misbehave and report wrong free memory (or cause Xid). That would explain why nvidia-smi on host shows normal free memory but the process sees OOM.

Attempts to mitigate (and results):
- Removed /usr/local/cuda-12.0 from image (rebuild): new image didn't show failure on prod-gpu-12 for ~10 runs, then flaked once.
- Forced LD_LIBRARY_PATH inside container to point to host libs (LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu) using docker --env: reduced failures but not eliminated.
- Docker option --privileged? tried in dev: not allowed for prod.
- Swapped to another base image (nvidia/cuda:12.2-runtime) -> reproducible behavior changed, fewer Xid 79 but occasional OOMs remained.

Things that did NOT help (useful negative data):
- Reinstalling driver on host (apt purge && apt install nvidia-driver-535) did not consistently fix the flakes (suggests host driver likely ok).
- Upgrading python packages (latest torch wheel 2.2.0) in image did not fix.

What looked promising:
- Running python with LD_PRELOAD set to host libcuda path inside container prevented the allocation mismatch in 20/20 quick trials. Command tested:
  LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 python -c "import torch; [torch.empty(40_000_000, dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda') for _ in range(3)]"
  -> completed without OOMs on prod-gpu-12 in my trials.

Remaining unknowns / open questions:
- Why does shared object resolution pick the container-local compat libs in some runs and host libs in others? Race condition between rpath and LD_LIBRARY_PATH? docker/nvidia-container-toolkit mounting behavior?
- Could multiple python worker processes and forking change which lib is seen first? (we saw different outcomes when using gunicorn with preload vs without).
- Are there stale LD_PRELOAD settings in our systemd unit or exec wrapper?

Next investigation steps (TODO):
- Add deterministic repro: small C program that calls cuInit and cudaMalloc and prints which libcuda.so was used (dlopen + dladdr). Run across hosts and images.
- Audit image build: run 'grep -R "cuda" /usr/local' and check leftover compatibility symlinks. Stop packing any libcuda* into images. Create CI check that fails builds if libcuda is present.
- Add process startup wrapper that logs LD_LIBRARY_PATH and ldd of python binary to logs for first 30s after container start.
- Re-run with strace + LD_DEBUG=libs on a failing run to capture exact open order (pipe output to S3).
- Try changing container runtime to nvidia-container-toolkit 2.12 (if available) on one maintenance host to see difference.

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- If nvidia-smi shows plenty of free memory but process gets OOM: suspect library mismatch (libcudart/libcuda) before assuming allocation logic bug.
- LD_PRELOADing host libcuda consistently forces correct driver-bind and can be used as a canary patch while we clean images. Not ideal long-term but useful in emergency.
- Watch for Xid 79 in dmesg (GPU fallen off the bus) — that's a hard failure and usually points to driver/kernel or PCI issues; however, mixed lib versions can also trigger driver panic.

Scratch commands to re-run later (copy-paste):
- docker run --rm --gpus all -e LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 registry.redwood.internal/rt-inference:v2026-02-10 \n  bash -c "python -c "import torch; [torch.empty(40_000_000, device='cuda') for _ in range(3)]""

- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import ctypes, os; print(os.environ.get('LD_LIBRARY_PATH')); ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1');"

- small C repro (compile on host and inside image) to print dladdr info for libcuda handle.

Final quick plan to ship a short-term fix:
1) CI block: fail build if any libcuda or libcudart files are present in the image. (PR in pipeline).
2) Add LD_PRELOAD env var to k8s pod spec for failing service as emergency rollback.
3) Schedule controlled host update to try nvidia-container-toolkit 2.12 and test.

If this becomes a customer-facing incident we should prepare a note: brief timeline, impact, mitigation (LD_PRELOAD + image rebuild), and next steps (CI block + proper base images).

Random breadcrumbs / links found during triage:
- https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker/issues/2168 (libcuda in image issues)
- https://devtalk.nvidia.com/default/topic/ *archived threads about Xid 79 and driver shimming*

End of scratchpad. Will update with C repro and CI PR link.
